findings.title: Removing values from V also changes training, prediction, and saved-state compatibility
findings.detail:
The ruling needs an explicit decision about identity compatibility. refusal controls both saving and H-0138 identity: identity_eligible sends an entire column to pandas when any category leaves V, while category_identity_key rejects previously fitted categories that leave V.

Executed tiny regression models used two folds, three trees, OMP_NUM_THREADS=4, and an in-memory refusal substitution marking the reported value outside V. On NumPy 2.2.6/pandas 2.3.3, a column containing [v, Decimal(1), np.int8(1), 'x'] currently fits and predicts; with that substitution, fit raises TypeError('argument must be an integer') on the pandas path. A simple [v, 'x'] column still fits and gives the same measured predictions, but identity_columns changes from ['c'] to [], fit emits the unsaveable-value warning, and both export surfaces change from passing preflight to SERIALIZATION_FAILED. These are conditional consequences of refusing v on both lanes; the runtime-exact predicate continues admitting this seconds-unit example on NumPy 2.x.

Compatibility is also affected without refitting. On NumPy 2.2.6, an original model passed check_category_values and its real fitted results survived compressed joblib serialization in BytesIO with v intact. After the refusal substitution, Model.load's rehydration succeeded when supplied those deserialized results in memory, but predict raised TypeError('no category identity key for a value outside V (frozenset)'). Loading encoder state never reclassifies its recorded identity_columns. On NumPy 1.24, an equivalent manually serialized keyed state restored two members and originally produced codes [0, 1]; the runtime-exact new refusal made its transform raise the same TypeError.

Thus current NumPy 2.x exports can contain this value; current NumPy 1.24 public exports cannot pass preflight. Existing exported projects carry their own frozen implementation and are unaffected by changing the installed library. Disk export/load was unavailable in this sandbox; the joblib projection and Model.load rehydration were measured separately. A cross-lane joblib experiment failed earlier with the existing numpy._core import incompatibility, so it supplies no cross-lane compatibility guarantee.

Recommendation: retain the existing identity domain for fitted-state lookup and make the new refusal a saving restriction. Otherwise the owner must explicitly accept changed training behavior and late prediction failures for existing keyed states, and update H-0138's contract accordingly.

findings.title: Specify runtime-dependent versus portable refusal, and avoid public round trips in the predicate
findings.detail:
An exact implementable rule is: perform today's complete type, scalar, timezone, and depth validation first; then project the validated tree through the codec without invoking public encode/decode. Project scalar leaves using the private codec operations, preserve tuple positions, and construct each projected frozenset in the canonical member order _encode writes. Refuse if any such construction reduces that node's member count. Carry the projection upward so outer sets also detect collisions between tuple or frozenset members. This covers arbitrary larger sets and nesting using the actual runtime's behavior, rather than a list of known scalar pairs. Expected projection failures must become a refusal reason rather than escape from refusal.

That rule is closed for actual collapse on the running implementation, including changes to NumPy equality or hashing, but its answer is version-dependent. For the reported seconds-unit value it refuses on 1.24 and admits on 2.2.6 and 2.4.2. Identical answers on both lines are an additional product requirement, not a consequence of the ruling's wording. I recommend runtime-exact refusal, documenting that policy and preserving identity compatibility as described above. If the owner instead requires portable admissibility, define the portable collision semantics explicitly; a finite measured blacklist does not establish closure across NumPy versions.

The static candidate 'decoded members compare equal' is not the exact collapse condition: on NumPy 2.x, int(4) == timedelta64(4, 's') is still true, but their different hashes allow both set members to remain. A direct uint64/timedelta blacklist is also incomplete for structural members.

Executed predicate prototypes demonstrate the cost distinction. Calling public encode on the same value from _refusal caused RecursionError. Public member-wise calls terminate, but repeatedly invoke validation: an admitted depth-eight singleton-frozenset chain took approximately 17,255/17,063 microseconds on NumPy 1.24/2.2.6, versus 2.50/2.38 microseconds today. Private whole-subtree projection at each set took 115/112 microseconds. A bottom-up prototype preserving canonical write order took approximately 17.6/17.5 microseconds. For a safe three-member set it took 8.2/7.9 microseconds versus roughly 2.8/3.0 today; for 100 integer members, 193/192 versus roughly 86. These were minimum-of-three timeit measurements. A direct static scan added roughly one microsecond for the reported pair, but missed structural cases. The bottom-up approach retains codec sorting costs and linear auxiliary storage; public member-wise re-entry multiplies work with nesting.

findings.title: The measured reach includes NumPy 2.x and collisions between structural members
findings.detail:
Executed the scalar/temporal matrix on NumPy 1.24.0/pandas 2.0.0 and NumPy 2.2.6/pandas 2.3.3. It covered every _NUMPY_PLAIN type: bool_, int8/int16/int32/int64, uint8/uint16/uint32/uint64, float32/float64, str_; additionally Python int/float/bool/complex/Decimal, NumPy complex64/complex128, and Python/NumPy strings and bytes. Numeric probes included 0, 1, and 4. Temporal counterparts included timedelta64 units Y, M, W, D, h, m, s, ms, us, ns, ps, fs, as, generic, 2s, and 15m; datetime64 units and multiples; pd.Timedelta, datetime.timedelta, pd.Timestamp, datetime.datetime, and datetime.date.

At matched raw counts on 1.24, uint64 was the only measured scalar family newly losing a member, for every tested timedelta64 unit. Plain int/bool and NumPy bool/signed integers/uint8/uint16/uint32 were already coalesced during source-set construction; they did not newly collapse during decoding. Float, complex, string, and bytes families survived without new collapse. Decimal/timedelta64 pairs at those matching hashes raised TypeError during source-set construction, so there was no frozenset value to classify. No measured scalar paired with datetime64 or the pandas/Python temporal families newly collapsed.

On 2.2.6, uint64 with month-unit timedelta64 still collapsed at counts 0, 1, and 4; year-unit count 0 also collapsed. Other tested fixed-unit pairs retained their members. Generic timedelta64 is unhashable on that line, so those sets cannot be constructed. The same calendar-unit results and successful seconds-unit reproducer were confirmed with NumPy 2.4.2/pandas 3.0.1. Calendar durations remain relevant to V even though H-0139 separately refuses them at fit.

Additional scalar/scalar grids, including float32 versus float, bool_ versus int, str_ versus str, bytes_ versus bytes, complex versus float, 0.1, and integer precision boundaries, found no new collapses among 10,296 pairs on 1.24 and 8,385 constructible pairs on 2.2.6. Temporal/temporal testing covered 5,778 pairs per line and found no collapse. On 2.2.6, 321 ValueErrors and 30 OverflowErrors occurred during source-set construction, before codec projection. These are finite measurements, not an exhaustive proof over all numeric values or future NumPy versions.

Structural reach is essential. On 1.24, the reported pair became 2→1, adding 'x' became 3→2, and {uint64(4), timedelta64(4,'s'), timedelta64(4,'ms')} became 3→1. Both frozenset({(uint64(4),), (timedelta64(4,'s'),)}) and a set of the corresponding singleton frozensets became 2→1. A bad frozenset inside a tuple inside an outer frozenset failed despite the outer member count remaining unchanged. The seconds-unit structural examples survived on 2.2.6. A bare tuple (uint64(4), timedelta64(4,'s')) retained both positions and round-tripped on both lines: tuples are affected through contained sets or by becoming equal members of an enclosing set, not by positional deduplication.

The top-level category list must remain separate. For [uint64(4), timedelta64(4,'s'), 'x'], JSON projection retained list length 3 on both lines, but converting the decoded list to set produced size 2 on 1.24 and 3 on 2.2.6. _encoder_through_json and codegen preserve lists. Non-keyed consumers do use sets and pandas uniqueness checks, including categorical_encoder.py:242–245. Measured keyed preflight passed on both lines; removing the identity marker produced a JSON 'raises'/ValueError verdict on 1.24. A frozenset refusal must not accidentally reject these working keyed columns or undo H-0143.

findings.title: The generated implementation and every refusal consumer need coordinated behavior
findings.detail:
Changing only core refusal leaves the standalone implementation inconsistent. Generated _in_v determines admissibility by calling its own _encode_value; it never calls library refusal. Executed _in_v(v) returned True and _identity_key(v) produced a key on both lanes. Therefore the generated encoder, its decoder's re-encoding check, identity eligibility, and prediction lookup need an explicit matching policy. Keep a private unchecked projection operation so adding the guard does not create another recursion loop. Existing project copies must be distinguished from newly generated code.

The consumer trace is: core encode turns the new refusal into SERIALIZATION_FAILED with type/reason; decode checks refusal on the restored value and then canonical form, wrapping failures as DESERIALIZATION_FAILED with reason; category_identity_key raises TypeError; identity_eligible changes the builder and encoder routing. codegen.values.category_value supplies SERIALIZATION_FAILED with where/type/reason. exporter.unsaveable_category_values checks categories and modes, its fit warning reports once per column, and warn_saved_state_changes skips the H-0136 projection when an unsaveable saved or declared value is found. check_category_values rejects saved categories/modes and declared categories before reaching joblib/JSON behavioral checks, then the adapter checks. Model.export, public persistence.export, and export_code share this gate.

Measured after refusing v on each lane: simple-column fit warned; Model.export and export_code both raised SERIALIZATION_FAILED before path creation, with context column='c', type='frozenset', state='refit', and the displayed value. The existing exporter context does not include reason, although the message does. Thus the new outcome is early V refusal rather than an H-0136/H-0143 serializer/kind verdict. Unaffected keyed category-list examples continued passing behavioral preflight.

Loading is different: loader.py:464 unpickles encoder categories without running the export V gate. Declared-category metadata separately goes through decode at loader.py:163 and can fail with DESERIALIZATION_FAILED and path/key/reason. With runtime-exact refusal, the old seconds-unit JSON still decoded on 2.2.6 and still failed canonical decoding on 1.24. A portable rule must explicitly specify treatment of the decoded {int, timedelta64} form, whose uint64 provenance has disappeared.

Executed convert_pipeline_state followed by the real generated decoder and _keyed_codes entirely in memory: on 2.2.6 the artifact retained two categories, its frozenset retained two members, and generated codes were [0, 1]; on 1.24 generated decoding raised ValueError. Full generated-project execution involving model files could not run without writable storage.

findings.title: Correct the issue's failure location and its fit-time description
findings.detail:
Most of the reproducer is verified: on NumPy 1.24.0/pandas 2.0.0, v has two members, refusal(v) is None, encode writes integer 4 plus a timedelta64 tag, and decode raises DESERIALIZATION_FAILED for noncanonical reconstruction. Both hash to 4 and the decoded set has one member. The specific seconds-unit round trip succeeds on NumPy 2.2.6 and 2.4.2.

The issue's attribution to lizyml/codegen/values.py is false. That file is the library-side writer: executed category_value(v, where="categories of column 'c'") successfully returned the tagged object on both lanes. The generated ValueError comes from _decode_value in codegen/templates.py:213, specifically its canonical re-encoding comparison.

Also, the current failure is observable during Model.fit, not only when exporting. On the lowest lane, a 32-row, two-fold, three-tree model raised DESERIALIZATION_FAILED from the post-fit warn_saved_state_changes call. Fit had already committed its results: a subsequent predict succeeded and returned [0.4628942496527121, 0.46589125030748013] for the first two rows. Both export surfaces then raised the same DESERIALIZATION_FAILED. With the new refusal, the simple model instead returns from fit with a warning and export raises SERIALIZATION_FAILED. Record that before/after behavior in the proposal.

All probes imported this workspace's lizyml/__init__.py, used -B and OMP_NUM_THREADS=4, and printed the package path and versions. The digest snapshot lacks generated lizyml._version metadata, so it was supplied solely as an in-memory module. The exact 2.4.2/3.0.1 check used read-only package-path layering from the available environments.

findings.title: The existing populations have zero firing rate, so acceptance needs explicit new cases
findings.detail:
Executed firing-rate replay for the runtime-exact rule found 0/113 admitted SAMPLES values and 0/12,769 admitted category occurrences from all SAMPLES singles and pairs on each lane. These pairs are category lists, not newly constructed frozensets. Replaying all H-0138 probe IDs gave 0/13,029. The frozen oracle's encoder-case input replay gave 0/3,371 admitted occurrences on 1.24 and 0/3,315 on 2.2.6; temporal-case replay gave 0/9,633 on each. Seven ordinary-input missing occurrences per encoder replay were outside V and excluded from those denominators. A passive core-test census recorded 0/364 admitted root refusal calls on each lane.

With the runtime refusal applied in memory, the core category-values and generated-codec-copy tests passed unchanged: 553 passed, 1 deselected on each lane. The deselected hash-seed subprocess test cannot inherit the in-memory _version module. No existing expectation changed in this executed population. A full-suite census was not run: pytest's initial default capture attempt failed with 'No usable temporary directory'; the selected tests ran using -s and no cache provider. These numbers must not be described as a full-suite census.

As a separate adversarial expansion, constructing frozensets from all 6,328 SAMPLES pairs left 6,216 admitted sets after depth exclusions. The new rule fired on 13/6,216 on 1.24: uint64[1], value 4, paired with each of the thirteen base timedelta64 units. It fired on 1/6,216 on 2.2.6: the month-unit pair. This directly demonstrates the existing coverage gap.

Acceptance should require: both NumPy lines; every scalar/temporal family above; zero and nonzero calendar cases; unit multiples and generic-unit construction limits; numeric/string/bytes controls; larger sets and both insertion orders; tuple members, frozenset members, nested offending sets, and depth boundaries; unchanged top-level category lists and H-0143 verdicts; generated/library agreement for encoding, decoding, and identity eligibility; and rejection before any output is written.

Assert refusal reasons, core encode SERIALIZATION_FAILED with type/reason, codegen writer SERIALIZATION_FAILED with where/type/reason, and export refusal with column/value/type/state for refit, individual folds, last-fold fallback, modes, and unused declared categories. Preserve malformed-input DESERIALIZATION_FAILED with reason and declared-load path/key context; standalone generated code uses ValueError. Add tiny-model coverage for warnings, fit routing, prediction, old keyed states, and existing exported-project behavior under the selected lane policy.

Update BLUEPRINT's V definition at 1948, identity coupling at 1957, and codec description at 1996; update HISTORY's H-0133 P1/P2 references and document the compatibility decision. The owner should approve those semantics before implementation is judged complete.
